$comment: Classification of every rule id emitted by any tool during the benchmark run.
bucket:  hazard   = names a structural production risk. The only bucket counted
toward loose detection and false positives.
hygiene  = session settings and re-runnability. Not counted.
advisory = soft preference or design advice. Not counted.
info     = the tool describing a statement it considers safe. Not counted.
hazards: which corpus hazard slugs this rule's message actually names. Used for
strict detection, independently of bucket — so a hygiene-bucket rule that
names the missing-lock-timeout hazard still earns credit on the file that
asserts it, without polluting the false-positive count.
A rule gets a hazard slug only if its own message names that hazard. 'The tool
flagged the file' is loose detection and is measured separately.
Written from each rule's emitted message text and its published documentation.
Anything you disagree with is a one-line diff here, and the numbers move with it.

MP002.note: SET NOT NULL requires a full scan; recommends the CHECK pattern.

MP003.note: Fires on the volatile default. Its message claims no rewrite occurs on PG17, which contradicts the ALTER TABLE manual and handbook MPH-006 — see the defects section of RESULTS.md. Credited for firing; the wrong message is reported separately.

MP004.note: Names the lock-queue hazard, but the remedy is a session setting, so it is hygiene for false-positive purposes.

MP006.note: VACUUM FULL rewrite under ACCESS EXCLUSIVE.

MP008.note: Multiple DDL statements sharing one transaction, so locks accumulate.

MP009.note: DROP INDEX without CONCURRENTLY. A real hazard, not one this corpus asserts.

MP010.note: Names the client breakage, not just the lock.

MP011.note: UPDATE without WHERE in one transaction; names WAL and lock duration.

MP012.note: ALTER TYPE ADD VALUE inside a transaction.

MP016.note: Suggests indexing the referencing column. Design advice, not a lock hazard in the migration itself.

MP018.note: Second SET NOT NULL rule; same hazard as MP002.

MP022.note: Names CASCADE and the silent dependent drops.

MP026.note: DROP TABLE generally. Credited for the corpus's DROP TABLE CASCADE file even though it does not single out CASCADE — the merge is blocked either way.

MP027.note: UNIQUE constraint built inline under ACCESS EXCLUSIVE.

MP028.note: Names query, view and FK breakage.

MP045.note: Table created without a primary key. Design advice.

MP046.note: DETACH without CONCURRENTLY locks the parent.

MP052.note: Type change may break dependent views and functions. A distinct hazard from the rewrite; not asserted by this corpus.

MP054.note: The new enum value used in the same transaction that added it.

MP055.note: Primary key dropped without repointing REPLICA IDENTITY.

MP058.note: Claims repeated ACCESS EXCLUSIVE acquisitions across separate ALTER TABLE statements on one table. Scored as a hazard claim; on the handbook's own NOT VALID patterns its advice to combine the statements is wrong, and that shows up as a false positive.

MP061.note: Column ordering to reduce alignment padding.

MP062.note: Stored generated column forces a full rewrite.

MP064.note: Names the FK-enforcement and replication consequences, not just the lock.

MP069.note: Notes that an FK locks both tables and asks for lock_timeout on both. Remedy is a session setting.

MP070.note: CONCURRENTLY build with no preceding DROP INDEX IF EXISTS, so a retry can inherit an invalid index.

MP071.note: Second rename rule; names view, function and trigger breakage.

MP072.note: ATTACH scans the default partition under ACCESS EXCLUSIVE.

MP074.note: FK is not DEFERRABLE. Preference, not a hazard in the migration.

MP080.note: Data change mixed into a DDL migration file. Organisational advice.

MP086.note: Foreign key has no explicit ON DELETE clause. NO ACTION is a valid deliberate choice, so this is a be-explicit preference rather than a production hazard — same treatment as MP074, MP016 and pgfence's fk-missing-index.

MP088.note: Backfill not followed by ANALYZE. A real operational point, but the consequence is stale planner statistics rather than a lock, rewrite, blocking scan or blast radius, so it does not meet the hazard bar this benchmark uses. It fires on the handbook's own correctly batched backfill.

MP090.note: Row-level trigger creation: names the SHARE ROW EXCLUSIVE lock and the per-row cost on every future write. Structurally the same claim as pgfence's create-trigger, which is scored as a hazard, so this is scored the same way — and it costs us the same two false positives on the handbook's expand/contract sync triggers.

MP094.note: ATTACH without a matching CHECK, so the bound is validated by a full scan under ACCESS EXCLUSIVE on both tables. States MPH-019 more precisely than MP072.

MP097.note: DROP INDEX against a constraint-backed index, which PostgreSQL rejects outright — a runtime failure claim, same class as the CONCURRENTLY-in-transaction error. Correct on safe/s06 (it caught a genuine bug in this corpus); wrong on agent-flavored/a08, where the index is never adopted as a constraint. That over-inference is reported in the defects section.

adding-field-with-default.note: Covers both rewrite triggers; message names the ACCESS EXCLUSIVE rewrite and the PG11+ non-volatile exemption.

adding-foreign-key-constraint.note: Names the scan and the SHARE ROW EXCLUSIVE lock on both tables.

adding-not-nullable-field.note: SET NOT NULL blocks reads during the scan.

adding-serial-primary-key-field.note: PK added inline under ACCESS EXCLUSIVE. Real hazard, not one this corpus asserts as a slug.

ban-drop-table.note: DROP TABLE generally. Credited on the CASCADE file for the same reason as MP026.

ban-truncate-cascade.note: Names the recursive truncation through foreign keys.

constraint-missing-not-valid.note: Generic 'new constraints scan the table' rule; covers both constraint hazards in this corpus.

disallowed-unique-constraint.note: UNIQUE built inline under ACCESS EXCLUSIVE.

prefer-robust-stmts.note: Re-runnability. Fires on most of the corpus.

prefer-text-field.note: varchar-to-text preference. Fires on the varchar-widening context file.

require-concurrent-index-deletion.note: DROP INDEX without CONCURRENTLY. Not a slug this corpus asserts.

require-enum-value-ordering.note: About BEFORE/AFTER placement of the new value. Never mentions transactions, so it earns no credit for the enum-in-transaction hazard even though it fires on those files.

add-column-constant-default.note: LOW; explicitly says the operation is instant and metadata-only on PG11+.

add-column-non-constant-default.note: HIGH; names the rewrite under ACCESS EXCLUSIVE.

add-constraint-check-not-valid.note: LOW; describes the safe NOT VALID form as a brief metadata operation.

add-constraint-unique-using-index.note: LOW; describes the safe USING INDEX adoption.

add-pk-without-using-index.note: HIGH; PK built inline. Not a slug this corpus asserts.

alter-enum-add-value.note: LOW, and it fires identically on the safe standalone ALTER TYPE file, so it does not discriminate between the hazard and its fix. Credited for strict detection anyway because the message does state that the new value cannot be used in the same transaction; bucketed info so it raises no false positive on the safe file. The non-discrimination is called out in RESULTS.md.

alter-enum-no-ordering.note: LOW; BEFORE/AFTER placement, same scope as Squawk's require-enum-value-ordering.

attach-partition.note: HIGH; names the validation scan and both locks.

concurrent-in-transaction.note: error; states it will fail at runtime.

create-index-not-concurrent.note: MEDIUM; names the SHARE lock and blocked writes.

create-trigger.note: MEDIUM lock claim on CREATE TRIGGER. Kept as a hazard because SHARE ROW EXCLUSIVE genuinely blocks writes; it fires on the handbook's own expand/contract sync triggers, which is why it appears in the false-positive table. Defensible flag, still a flag.

detach-partition.note: HIGH; names the ACCESS EXCLUSIVE on the parent.

detach-partition-concurrent.note: LOW; describes the safe CONCURRENTLY form as non-blocking.

drop-constraint.note: MEDIUM; generic ACCESS EXCLUSIVE claim on any DROP CONSTRAINT. Says nothing about replica identity, so it earns no credit for the replication hazard.

drop-index-not-concurrent.note: MEDIUM. Not a slug this corpus asserts.

drop-table.note: CRITICAL; credited on the CASCADE file for the same reason as MP026 and ban-drop-table.

enable-disable-trigger.note: LOW; reports only the SHARE ROW EXCLUSIVE lock. Never mentions that TRIGGER ALL also disables foreign-key enforcement, so no credit for the disable-trigger-all hazard.

fk-missing-index.note: LOW; suggests indexing the referencing column, same scope as MP016.

lock-timeout-after-dangerous-statement.note: error, but the subject is where the timeout setting sits relative to the DDL.

missing-lock-timeout.note: Same treatment as MP004 and require-lock-timeout.

prefer-robust-create-index.note: Asks for IF NOT EXISTS on a concurrent build. Handbook MPH-012 argues the opposite — IF NOT EXISTS reports success over an invalid index — which is discussed in RESULTS.md.

rename-column.note: LOW; calls the rename instant metadata-only and never mentions that running clients break. No credit for the rename hazard.

rename-table.note: HIGH; explicitly names broken queries, views and foreign keys.

statement-after-access-exclusive.note: Names lock accumulation across statements in one transaction.

update-in-migration.note: Names the unbatched bulk backfill and recommends batching out of band.

vacuum-full.note: HIGH; names the rewrite and the lock duration.

validate-constraint.note: LOW; describes the safe validation as a non-blocking SHARE UPDATE EXCLUSIVE scan.
